---
# ONE source file -> three outputs (07_report_and_post_templates.md):
#   (1) blog post            report.html   (format: html, sections A1-A8)
#   (2) LinkedIn post        output/linkedin_post.txt + output/linkedin_check.txt (section B)
#   (3) technical note, 2-3 pages A4, brief.pdf (format: typst, section C): the place for more detail
# Every number comes from output/key_numbers.csv through kn(); an unknown key stops the render.
title: "How far did Indonesia's cooking-oil price move away from its usual link to world palm oil prices during the 2022 export curbs?"
description: "Over January-May 2022 as a whole, the data show no clear shift; the gap narrowed while retail caps applied and widened once packaged-oil caps were lifted."
author: "Pietro Sala"
date: "2026-11-26"
categories: ["Region: SE Asia", "Method: Time series", "Theme: WB"]
image: output/fig1_hero.png           # listing thumbnail + open-graph image
draft: true                           # set to false to publish
title-block-banner: true
params:
  linkedin_max_chars: 1300
  linkedin_hook_max_chars: 210        # approx. text visible before "...see more" on mobile
  strict: false                       # true = stop the render if LinkedIn limits are exceeded
format:
  html:
    toc: false
    format-links: false
  typst:
    output-file: brief                # -> brief.pdf
    papersize: a4
    margin:
      x: 1.7cm
      y: 1.4cm
    fontsize: 11pt
    fig-format: png
    keep-typ: false
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r}
#| label: guard
#| include: false
# Before the analysis has been run there are no results: stop knitting here, so the
# website build on GitHub does not fail while a case is still in progress.
if (!file.exists("output/key_numbers.csv")) knitr::knit_exit("*Results pending.*")
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(acutils)
  library(yaml)
})
meta    <- yaml::read_yaml("00_meta.yml", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
kn_file <- "output/key_numbers.csv"
k <- function(key, ...) acutils::kn(key, file = kn_file, ...)   # formatted key number
kn_tbl  <- acutils::kn_read(kn_file)
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a) || identical(a, "")) b else a
bold_first <- function(x) unname(vapply(x, function(s) {   # PDF: bold the first sentence, or its lead clause if long
  sent <- sub("^(.+?[.:])( .*|)$", "\\1", s, perl = TRUE)
  lead <- sent
  if (length(strsplit(sent, " ")[[1]]) > 16) {
    cl <- sub("^(.+?[,;])( .*|)$", "\\1", s, perl = TRUE)
    if (cl != s) lead <- cl
  }
  paste0("**", lead, "**", substring(s, nchar(lead) + 1))
}, ""))
bullets  <- function(x) cat(paste0("- ", x), sep = "\n")
site_url <- "https://mithril-metrics.github.io"   # same for both authors
case_id  <- meta$id %||% basename(getwd())
blog_url <- meta$links$blog %||% paste0(site_url, "/cases/", case_id, "/report.html")
code_url <- meta$links$code %||% paste0("https://github.com/Mithril-Metrics/mithril-metrics.github.io/tree/main/cases/", case_id)
```

```{r}
#| label: shared-text
#| include: false
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WRITE HERE ONCE. These strings feed the blog, the technical note (PDF) and the LinkedIn post.
# Note-only strings (more detail than the blog): method_detail, robustness, references.
method_detail <- "PLACEHOLDER: **one bolded sentence on what we compare.** Then *Data.*, *Model.*, *Inference.*, *Identification.* as short italic-labelled parts. 120-200 words."
results_note <- c("PLACEHOLDER: **bolded key finding.** Then the estimate and its interval from kn(), in one or two short sentences.")
robustness <- c("PLACEHOLDER: **bolded lead: what the check shows.** Then each check with its estimate and interval from kn().")
references <- c("PLACEHOLDER: Author, A. (year). Title. *Outlet*. [link text](https://...)",
                "PLACEHOLDER: one reference per element; each prints on its own line.")
# Use k("key") for every number (k("key", unit = TRUE) adds the unit, abs = TRUE drops sign).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
question <- meta$question
pct <- function(key, ...) paste0(k(key, ...), "%")
ci <- function(lo, hi) paste0("95% CI ", pct(lo), " to ", pct(hi))

bottom_line <- paste0(
  "Over January-May 2022 as a whole, our pre-specified test finds no clear shift in Indonesia's retail ",
  "cooking-oil price relative to its usual link with world palm oil (", pct("main_window_pct", sign = TRUE), ", ",
  ci("main_window_lo", "main_window_hi"), "). Split as planned, January-March shows no clear shift (",
  pct("r1_window_a_pct", sign = TRUE), ") and April-May ", pct("r1_window_b_pct", sign = TRUE),
  " (about Rp", k("r1_window_b_idr"), " per litre at 2021 prices), after the caps on packaged oil were lifted ",
  "in mid-March; monthly data cannot separate this from other shocks."
)

why_now <- paste0(
  "Indonesia's Trade Regulation 16/2026 routes crude palm oil exports through a single state-owned exporter: ",
  "a transition from June to December 2026, and the state exporter as sole exporter of record from 1 January 2027. ",
  "**The last time the government administered export flows was 2022**, when a one-price policy, a domestic supply ",
  "obligation, retail caps, an export quota, higher export levies and a four-week export ban followed each other ",
  "within five months. The 2027 scheme changes export channels rather than banning exports, so 2022 is a partial ",
  "analogue, but it is the closest record of how domestic cooking-oil prices respond when export flows are managed."
)

method_plain <- paste0(
  "**We ask how far the national retail price moved away from the level its usual relationship with world palm oil ",
  "would predict, in each phase of the 2022 measures, allowing for the fact that price gaps carry over from month to month.** ",
  "We use ", k("n_months"), " months of BPS national average retail prices (November 2020 to July 2026) and the world ",
  "crude palm oil price in rupiah, both from FAO's food price monitoring database. Retail cooking oil normally passes on ",
  "about a third of a world-price change within three months (elasticity ", k("passthrough_sum"), "), so the comparison is ",
  "with that link, not with world prices themselves: in January-May 2022 world palm oil in rupiah was ",
  pct("cpo_window_vs_2021_pct"), " above its 2021 average and retail cooking oil ", pct("vegoil_window_vs_2021_pct"),
  ". The test for January-May and the split into January-March and April-May were fixed before we saw results; ",
  "checks added afterwards are labelled exploratory."
)

implications <- c(
  paste0("If the aim of administering exports is lower domestic prices, **the 2022 record gives no evidence that national ",
         "average retail prices fall relative to their usual world-price link.** Producers may bear part of the cost: ",
         "farmers reported fresh-fruit-bunch prices roughly halving during the 2022 ban ",
         "([Al Jazeera, 16 May 2022](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2022/5/16/indonesian-farmers-decry-palm-oil-export-ban-as-prices-plummet)); ",
         "we do not measure this."),
  paste0("If retail caps are the instrument, the recorded gap narrowed only while caps applied and widened within weeks ",
         "of lifting them. The trade-off is availability: in February 2022 the national average was ",
         pct("vegoil_feb2022_vs_cap_pct"), " above the highest cap in force, consistent with the shortages the ",
         "[Ombudsman reported](https://ombudsman.go.id/news/download/temuan-ombudsman-soal-minyak-goreng-penimbunan-hingga-pengalihan-ke-pasar-tradisional) ",
         "in February, though we do not test this."),
  paste0("If the aim is to monitor the 2027 scheme, national monthly averages cannot separate measures that are weeks ",
         "apart; weekly prices by province and by product type (bulk vs packaged) would.")
)

caveats <- c(
  "The 2022 measures came within weeks of each other; **monthly data cannot isolate any one of them**, and January is partly treated.",
  paste0("The series is a national average that sat well above every cap (Rp", k("vegoil_feb2022"), " per litre in February 2022); ",
         "it does not show the price of capped oil, how much households could buy or regional differences (bulk oil cost ",
         "Rp14,250 to Rp29,250 per kg across provinces in May 2022, ",
         "[Katadata](https://katadata.co.id/berita/industri/6285dba47b70b/tiga-pekan-larangan-ekspor-cpo-harga-minyak-goreng-curah-dekati-het))."),
  "Indonesia's own measures moved the world palm oil price used as the benchmark, so in 2022 the predicted level is not a policy-free comparison.",
  paste0("The January-May estimate depends on how months are weighted and where the phase boundaries fall (",
         pct("main_window_pct", sign = TRUE), " pre-specified, ", pct("main_window_ols_pct", sign = TRUE),
         " with equal weights, ", pct("s7_lag1_window_pct", sign = TRUE), " with phases moved by one month)."),
  "One country and one episode; the result does not predict the effect of the 2027 state-exporter scheme."
)

findings <- c(                                   # LinkedIn arrows; finalised at P9
  paste0("Jan-May 2022 as a whole: ", pct("main_window_pct", sign = TRUE), ", not clearly different from zero"),
  paste0("Apr-May 2022, after packaged-oil caps were lifted: ", pct("r1_window_b_pct", sign = TRUE),
         ", about Rp", k("r1_window_b_idr"), " per litre"),
  paste0("Late 2021, before the 2022 measures: the gap had already widened by about ", pct("s4_pre3_pct"))
)

key_figures <- list(
  c(value = pct("main_window_pct", sign = TRUE), label = "Jan-May 2022, pre-specified test (not clear)"),
  c(value = pct("r1_window_b_pct", sign = TRUE), label = "Apr-May 2022, planned split"),
  c(value = paste0("Rp", k("r1_window_b_idr")), label = "Apr-May shift per litre, 2021 prices"),
  c(value = pct("s4_pre3_pct", sign = TRUE), label = "Oct-Dec 2021, before the 2022 measures (exploratory)")
)

author_slug <- gsub("[^a-z]+", "-", tolower(iconv(rmarkdown::metadata$author %||% "", to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT")))

method_tag <- "Method: interrupted time series with AR(1) errors on FAO GIEWS monthly prices, Nov 2020 - Jul 2026"
hashtags   <- "#FoodPolicy #PalmOil #Indonesia #AgriculturalEconomics"
```

## What the data show

### The gap widened sharply after packaged-oil caps were lifted

![](output/fig1_hero.png){fig-alt="Bar chart of the monthly gap between Indonesia's national retail cooking-oil price and the price predicted from world palm oil, November 2020 to July 2026. The gap is negative in early 2021, turns positive in late 2021, falls close to zero in February and March 2022 and peaks in April and May 2022 before settling at a smaller positive level." width="100%"}

**Split as planned, January-March 2022 shows no clear shift (`r pct("r1_window_a_pct", sign = TRUE)`), while April-May shows `r pct("r1_window_b_pct", sign = TRUE)` (`r ci("r1_window_b_lo", "r1_window_b_hi")`), about Rp`r k("r1_window_b_idr")` per litre at 2021 prices.** April came after the caps on packaged oil were lifted on 16 March and mostly before the export ban of 28 April. In an exploratory check, no two-month window elsewhere in the series shows a shift above `r pct("s5_max2")`.

### Over January-May as a whole, the answer depends on how months are weighted

![](output/figB_phase_effects.png){fig-alt="Point estimates with 95 percent intervals: January to May 2022 (pre-specified), January to March and April to May 2022 (planned split), from June 2022, and the wheat flour placebo. Only April to May lies clearly above zero." width="100%"}

**The pre-specified estimate is `r pct("main_window_pct", sign = TRUE)` (`r ci("main_window_lo", "main_window_hi")`), but it mainly compares January 2022 with December 2021.** Because price gaps carry over from month to month, the model weights January by `r k("w_window_jan2022")` and December 2021 by `r k("w_window_dec2021")`; no other month gets more than `r k("w_window_other_max")`. By December the gap had already widened by about `r pct("s4_pre3_pct")` (`r ci("s4_pre3_lo", "s4_pre3_hi")`, exploratory), before any of the 2022 measures. Weighting the five months equally gives `r pct("main_window_ols_pct", sign = TRUE)`, and moving the phase boundaries by one month gives `r pct("s7_lag1_window_pct", sign = TRUE)` (both exploratory). We therefore read the pre-specified result as "not clear", not as "no effect".

### Month by month, the moves line up with the caps

![](output/fig2_event_months.png){fig-alt="Monthly estimates with 95 percent intervals from October 2021 to December 2022. The estimate drops in February 2022, jumps in April 2022 and declines gradually from June onwards." width="100%"}

**In an exploratory month-by-month check, the gap fell `r k("s6_feb_minus_jan_pp", abs = TRUE)` points in February 2022, the first full month of retail caps, and rose `r k("s6_apr_minus_mar_pp")` points in April.** In May, when the export ban fell, it changed by `r k("s6_may_minus_apr_pp", sign = TRUE)` points. The timing matches the caps; it does not show that the caps caused the moves, and a four-week ban may not be visible in monthly averages.

```{r}
#| label: linkedin
#| include: false
# Section B: LinkedIn post, built from the same strings and key numbers.
hook <- paste0("Indonesia's 2022 cooking-oil price measures: the retail price moved with the caps, ",
               "not clearly over the whole period (", pct("main_window_pct", sign = TRUE), ").")
li <- paste0(
  hook, "\n\n",
  why_now, "\n\n",
  "What we found:\n", paste0("→ ", findings, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n",
  "What it means: ", implications[1], "\n\n",
  method_tag, "\n",
  "Full analysis and code: link in the first comment\n\n",
  hashtags
)
dir.create("output", showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(li, "output/linkedin_post.txt", useBytes = TRUE)
writeLines(paste0("Full analysis and code: ", blog_url), "output/linkedin_first_comment.txt", useBytes = TRUE)

n_total <- nchar(li, type = "chars")
n_hook  <- nchar(hook, type = "chars")
checks <- c(
  sprintf("LinkedIn post: %d characters (limit %d) %s", n_total, params$linkedin_max_chars,
          if (n_total <= params$linkedin_max_chars) "OK" else "TOO LONG"),
  sprintf("Hook: %d characters (aim <= %d, approx. visible before 'see more') %s", n_hook,
          params$linkedin_hook_max_chars,
          if (n_hook <= params$linkedin_hook_max_chars) "OK" else "TOO LONG"),
  sprintf("Placeholders left: %s", if (grepl("\\[|Placeholder", li)) "YES - edit before posting" else "none")
)
writeLines(checks, "output/linkedin_check.txt")
message(paste(checks, collapse = "\n"))
too_long <- n_total > params$linkedin_max_chars || n_hook > params$linkedin_hook_max_chars
if (too_long && isTRUE(params$strict)) stop(paste(checks, collapse = "\n"))
if (too_long) warning(paste(checks, collapse = "\n"))
```
